scope: Queued callback authority for ordinary driving, convoy and building FSMs
finding: QueueJob retains callbacks for a later scheduler tick independently of FSM lifetime. Step adapters checked owner/brain/epoch but could execute an already queued command path after the same FSM had ended unexpectedly. Existing start checks alone do not bind later execution.
executionContext: CortexQueueJob only appends/coalesces pending jobs; SchedulerTick executes later from CBA normally unscheduled. Therefore the handle is published before the callback check. No claim of intra-callback scheduler preemption or changed budget.
implementation: Each Step now requires a typed finite nonnegative current FSM handle and not completedFSM before its execution path. Handle0 remains valid.
Ended/invalid executor clears pending and marks the callback completed, returning-1 without command, cleanup, restart, deadline renewal or task cancellation.
Existing one-restart paths retain original driving/room/convoy journals. Convoy can retain the same brain; driving/building restart replaces the old brain, which still rejects stale callbacks.
Existing scheduler runtime/subsystem gates already reject disabled jobs; no duplicate global runtime guard was added.
remaining: Forced termination, late callback retirement, original-budget restart and eventual native control restoration require actual normal/HC game validation.
No change proves current CQB/mixed-convoy physical quality or measured performance.
Queue dependency reverse/full-hull parent clearance remains incomplete; automatic queue activation remains off.
